title: Concordance of Microbiological and Histopathological Examination of Bone Biopsies in Diagnosing Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis, a Systematic Review

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Concordance of Microbiological and Histopathological Examination of Bone Biopsies in Diagnosing Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis, a Systematic Review》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · jfa270223-sec-0020-p9】Despite advances in diagnostic modalities, there is a lack of high‐quality evidence clarifying the relative diagnostic accuracy, concordance, and clinical implications of histopathology versus microbiology. Ongoing studies, such as the DOMINO DFU multicentre cohort in the UK, aim to address this gap by evaluating diagnostic pathways and their impact on outcomes [31].

【Aims and Objectives · jfa270223-sec-0030-p1】This systematic review aims to critically evaluate and compare the diagnostic concordance and clinical utility of microbiological analysis and histopathological examination of bone biopsy specimens in the diagnosis of diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO). Specifically, the objectives are to assess the diagnostic accuracy between microbiological findings and histopathology across multiple studies, determine the degree of diagnostic concordance between these two investigative modalities, and identify gaps within the current literature to propose recommendations for future research and for the development of improved clinical protocols regarding bone biopsy analysis in DFO.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Concordance of Microbiological and Histopathological Examination of Bone Biopsies in Diagnosing Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis, a Systematic Review》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · jfa270223-sec-0040-p1】A systematic review was conducted to evaluate the diagnostic concordance and accuracy of histopathological and microbiological analysis of bone biopsy specimens in diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO). Electronic databases searched included PubMed, Medline, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. The search covered articles published from January 2010 to June 2025 to reflect contemporary diagnostic standards and guidelines [29, 32]; (NICE 2019 [CG119 & NG19]) and the widespread adoption of multidisciplinary foot clinics in the UK.

【Methods · jfa270223-sec-0040-p6】Comparator: Comparative evaluation of histopathological and microbiological results from the same specimen or patient.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Concordance of Microbiological and Histopathological Examination of Bone Biopsies in Diagnosing Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis, a Systematic Review》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · jfa270223-sec-0050-p1】The initial search yielded 156 articles across MEDLINE, Google Scholar, PubMed, Cochrane, and CINAHL. Ultimately, 5 studies, published between 2010 and 2025, were included in the final synthesis. The complete selection process is illustrated in the PRISMA flowchart (Figure 1).

【Results · jfa270223-sec-0050-p5】Microbiological sensitivity ranged from 70% to 83.9%, specificity 25.8%–42%, and positive predictive values (PPV) were generally high (69%–92%). Negative predictive values (NPV) were consistently low (13%–44%).

Microbiological sensitivity ranged from 70% to 83.9%, specificity 25.8%–42%, and positive predictive values (PPV) were generally high (69%–92%). Negative predictive values (NPV) were consistently low (13%–44%).
